title: Zuckerberg Admits Meta Lacked AI Certainty on $200 Billion Bet
key_facts: Mark Zuckerberg, chief executive of Meta Platforms, said Meta had to commit to spending hundreds of billions of dollars last year on AI infrastructure before it knew whether its AI products would succeed (Bloomberg).

On the Cheeky Pint podcast, posted Monday 12 Oct, he recalled the line 'We're going to write this check for like, I don't know, $100 billion or $200 billion', and asking Alexandr Wang, Meta's chief AI officer, 'You sure this is going to work?'.
Wang said it was 'not clear at all that it was going to work', despite the 'obscenely large' sum (Hindustan Times).
Meta's chief financial officer Susan Li also warned about the cost of failure, Zuckerberg said (Hindustan Times).
Zuckerberg said he was not certain how consumers would respond to Muse, Meta's new personal AI assistant (Hindustan Times).
In its previous quarterly results Meta reported its lowest free cash flow in years and its shares fell 8% (Hindustan Times).
Meta reports its next results after the market closes on 21 Oct (Hindustan Times).
quote_evidence: 'We're going to write this check for like, I don't know, $100 billion or $200 billion,' Zuckerberg said on the Cheeky Pint podcast posted Monday.
'You sure this is going to work?' he recalled asking Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang.
Wang said it was 'not clear at all that it was going to work', despite the 'obscenely large' amount of money Meta was investing.
why_it_matters_hint: A chief executive admits the biggest AI spending commitment in his company's history was made without proof it would work, a week before Meta reports results.
event_date: Podcast posted Monday 12 Oct 2026; Bloomberg report 13 Oct 2026.
notes: The Bloomberg page gave only its first paragraphs (505 characters; paywall). The rest comes from the Hindustan Times, which reports the same podcast. The podcast itself was not opened.
